lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: theorems about triangles and their centers
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: theorems about triangles and their centers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: A parallelogram has an angle of 110°. Find the consecutive angle.
Third side is 18. Find the midsegment.

steps: Midsegment is half the third side.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A proof concludes that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: Every quadrilateral has diagonals that bisect each other.
The diagonals are perpendicular, which forces bisection.
Alternate interior angles give two pairs of congruent angles, and the opposite sides are congruent, so the triangles formed are congruent by ASA.
The diagonals are congruent, so they must bisect each other.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 116°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.
In a triangle, the two remote interior angles measure 40° and 46°. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In a parallelogram, one angle measures 107°. Find the consecutive angle.
In a triangle, a segment joins the midpoints of two sides. The third side measures 18. Find the length of the midsegment and state its relationship to the third side.
choices: 9, and it is perpendicular to the third side
9, and it is parallel to the third side
36, and it is parallel to the third side
18, and it is parallel to the third side

items.prompt: A proof concludes that vertical angles are congruent. Which statement supplies the missing justification?
choices: The two lines are parallel, forcing the angles to match.
Vertical angles are congruent by definition.
Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle, so both have the same measure.
The angles are congruent because they are opposite in position.

items.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 63°. Find the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.
